- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent history, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reverting trend.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% on day 2 post-spike.
- In 30-day horizon, model shows persistent bias toward higher values; apply downward adjustment of 1–4% for the first 5–7 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment history shows recent upward momentum, model tends to overreact; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high unless sentiment confirms strong bullish trend.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
